item.title: The hidden cost of India’s restriction on Bangladeshi visas
item.description: Since the August 2024 political upheaval in Bangladesh, India has restricted most visas for Bangladeshis, weakening people-to-people ties between the two countries and causing broader economic consequences.

item.title: The peacemakers: Meet Venezuelans who are fighting to free political detainees
item.description: In Venezuela, relatives and human-rights NGOs have stepped up calls for the immediate release of more than 800 victims of politically-motivated persecution of the government formerly led by Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: Pitching power: Unpacking the T20 Cricket World Cup crisis between Bangladesh and India
item.description: Bangladesh’s refusal to participate in 2026 T20 Cricket World Cup matches scheduled on Indian soil represents far more than a diplomatic standoff or a security dispute.

item.title: Meet Filip Ondrušek, the Austrian-Slavic chef who believes that local food reflects national history
item.description: “Modern reinterpretation of traditional dishes can maintain technical excellence while preserving the emotion, identity, and memories embedded in the food.”

item.title: Third World’s Stephen ‘Cat’ Coore, a Jamaican who straddled musical genres, dies at 69
item.description: Coore expanded the language of reggae, weaving roots with jazz, soul, funk, classical discipline and global sounds, while never losing Jamaica’s heartbeat. His guitar [...] spoke stories, unity, love and consciousness.

item.title: A Korean-Chinese women’s handmade Yanbian-style water tofu symbolizes family unity
item.description: When family members return home, tsodibi becomes the centerpiece of the meal — typically handmade by the women of the extended family, it symbolizes family unity and cooperation.

item.title: What does Tarique Rahman’s return after nearly 17 years in exile mean for Bangladesh?
item.description: Tarique Rahman’s return marks a defining moment for Bangladesh’s politics, energizing the Bangladesh Nationalist Party amid deep uncertainty, rising tensions, and an urgent search for democratic leadership.

item.title: Combating the climate crisis to promote peace in Mali
item.description: Between 1970 and 2020, the country experienced at least 40 major climate shocks, with drought affecting around 400,000 people each year and reducing crop revenues by US$9.5 million annually, according to the World Bank.

item.title: Venezuela inflates release figures as political prisoners remain in limbo
item.description: As Venezuelan authorities claim a mass release of political prisoners, families wait outside detention centers without answers, or guarantees. Behind the government’s discourse of reconciliation, uncertainty and fear persist.

item.title: Truth-telling and treaty: Australian Indigenous lawyer’s commitment to real change for First Nations People
item.description: "For me, cultural continuity is both a responsibility and a source of strength. It reminds me of why this work matters and who it is ultimately for."
